models.levels: thinking on (default) / off ("Instant mode"). No effort levels and no budget. preserve_thinking is a separate flag: it keeps earlier turns' reasoning in context and does not set effort.
models.mechanism: Chat-template kwarg `thinking`. When thinking is false, the generation prompt ends `<|im_assistant|>assistant<|im_middle|><think></think>`; otherwise (unset or true) it ends `...<|im_middle|><think>`. A second kwarg, `preserve_thinking` (default false), keeps historical <think>...</think> blocks instead of emptying them. There is no system-prompt line. I rendered the official template locally: passing reasoning_effort='low' leaves the prompt byte-identical to the default thinking prompt. The official API uses `thinking: {type: enabled|disabled, keep: null|all}` and lists `reasoning_effort` as "Not supported" for kimi-k2.6.
models.note: No K2.6 tech report exists; the HF card points to a blog. The K2.5 tech report (arXiv 2602.02276, which the K2.6 card cites for system prompts) says the model unifies thinking and instant modes, but it does not describe how the on/off switch was trained. The same report documents a 'budget-control reward' (Toggle) in RL for token efficiency. That shortens CoT in general; it is not a control users can set, and the report does not say whether it applies to K2.6. Moonshot's newer API models (kimi-k3, kimi-k3.1-pro) take reasoning_effort low/high/max, but K2.6 does not. Tinker lists it as type 'Hybrid + Vision', id moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 (32K) or moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6:peft:131072. In tinker_cookbook, kimi_k26 dispatches to KimiK25Renderer and kimi_k26_disable_thinking to KimiK25DisableThinkingRenderer, which prefills `<think></think>`.

models.levels: low / high / max (default max). Any other value, including medium, xhigh, or unset, silently becomes Max. Thinking cannot be turned off.
models.mechanism: Chat-template kwarg `reasoning_effort`. The template always emits `[gMASK]<sop><|system|>Reasoning Effort: Low|High|Max`, placed before any user system message, and the generation prompt always ends `<|assistant|><think>`. I rendered it locally: no kwarg -> 'Reasoning Effort: Max'; low -> 'Low'; high -> 'High'; medium and xhigh -> 'Max'. enable_thinking=False is ignored, so the prompt still opens <think>. `clear_thinking` (default false) only controls whether earlier reasoning is stripped. models.note: The control is a conditioning string in the prompt. Nothing cuts generation, so it is not an inference-time truncation trick. My inference, not documented: the model must have been post-trained on this string for it to work. No source describes how. The GLM-5.2 blog says GLM-5.2 'introduces effort level control'; GLM-5.3 shares GLM-5.2's base model, with only post-training added. The GLM-5.3 blog reports token use per level on Z.ai Code Bench: Max about 75K output tokens per task, High about 50K. The cited GLM-5 tech report (arXiv 2602.15763, v2 24 Feb 2026) does not mention reasoning effort. Tinker type is 'Reasoning'; only the 256K id is listed. For effort experiments: 'medium' is not a level and silently becomes Max, and low is the nearest thing to a no-thinking mode.

models.mechanism: A separate system message is inserted before the first non-system message, after any user system prompt: '<|message_system|><|content_text|>Thinking effort level: {x}<|end_message|>'. 3.1.3. Reasoning Control: Nemotron 3 Super is trained for three reasoning modes: reasoning-off, regular and low-effort. ... The low-effort reasoning mode is introduced during the SFT stage by adding training samples generated by GPT-OSS-120B in its low-effort mode (Du et al., 2025). These low-effort training samples cover the tasks of math reasoning, STEM question answering and instruction following, and represent 2% of the overall SFT data by sample count. ... We strip the reasoning traces from a random 3% samples for reasoning-off mode. After the main SFT stage, we add a short semi-on-policy SFT stage of 350 steps for inference-time budget control, where we collect roll-outs from the model and truncate 12% of reasoning traces to random reasoning budgets.

Low-effort Reasoning: During the multi-environmental RL stages, we convert a subset of the prompts to be in the low-effort mode. For each low-effort prompt, the reward for a roll-out is adjusted as a function of both correctness and the number of generated tokens. The low-effort prompt mix starts with subsets of Math, STEM QA and competitive coding prompts, in total representing 2% of all RL prompts being in low-effort mode, and is later reduced to subsets of Math and STEM QA, representing just 1% of RL prompts.

Mechanically, ``{reasoning effort: low}`` is appended to the last user message content; the generation suffix remains ``<think>\n`` ... This mode is only available on the Nemotron-3 Super model (NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16); the Nano and Ultra HF templates do not support ``low_effort``.

models.mechanism:
Chat-template kwarg reasoning_effort, used only when enable_thinking is unset or true. It adds a sentence to the system message, before any tool block and before user-supplied system text, and creates a system message if the conversation has none. xhigh (the default) adds 'Reasoning effort is set to xhigh. Please think carefully through the task, validate key assumptions, consider plausible alternatives, and prioritize correctness, consistency, and clarity in the final answer.' low adds 'Reasoning effort is set to low. Keep your thinking brief and focused, moving directly to the conclusion without unnecessary elaboration.' medium adds nothing, so a medium prompt is identical to Qwen3.6's default thinking prompt. No special tokens are involved. The generation prompt still ends '<|im_start|>assistant
<think>
'. enable_thinking=False prefills '<think>

</think>

' and adds no effort sentence. preserve_thinking now defaults to true. Tinker's renderers qwen3_8_xhigh_reasoning, qwen3_8_medium_reasoning and qwen3_8_low_reasoning inject the same sentences (REASONING_EFFORT_INSTRUCTIONS in qwen3_8.py), and qwen3_8_disable_thinking matches enable_thinking=False. The hosted Model Studio API differs: it maps reasoning_effort to a thinking_budget token cap (low=4096, medium=16384, xhigh=262144), and the cap is enforced by cutoff.
